Feeding
Patterns

Frequency
of
Eating

Landenberger
( 1968 )
reported
that
Pisaster
ochraceus
are

insatiable
feeders .
Data
from
experiments
on
the
clay
plates .

and
from
the
feeding
bowls
shows
that
Leptasterias
and
small

Pisaster
ochraceus
tend
to
have
eating
bouts
followed
by
spaces

that
range
from
two
to
four
or
more
days .
Figures
4
and
5
show

these
results .
Feder
( 1970 )
also
noted
" periods
when
individual

sea
stars
do
not
feed . "

The
animals
will
often
eat
more
than
one
item
a
day ,
in

fact
it
may
eat
two
or
three
in
quick
succession .
Dropping

the
shell
of
one
prey
item
and
quickly
securing
another
has

been
observed .
The
animals
often
move
while
eating
and
could

be
scanning
the
area
for
the
next
meal
or
possibly
making
a

determination
of
prey
density
which
might
influence
consumption .

Animals
that
are
presented
with
an
abundance
of
food
in

a
small
area ,
like
the
bowl
experiments ,
did
seem
to
eat
a

somewhat
larger
amount
than
those
on
the
plates .
So
the

frequency
of
contact
and
abundance
of
food
might
have
a
posi-

tive
effect
on
eating
response .

moving
quite
rapidly
on
occasion .

The
" hungry "
starfish

the
80
1

active

and

over

On
the

prey
is
abundant ,

area
that
the
starfish

usually

spot
and
eat
an
area

bare

easily
caught
prey
before

sea
table
experiment
provided
evidence
that
Leptasterias

and

an
area
with
abundant
prey ,

tend
to
stay

in

of

asteroids

near
or
